_staff: People of the team who write no code (testers, product owners). The redaction of personal data (R-02) keeps every git author and Jira user readable, and these names too; any other 'Name Surname' in ticket text is masked before a model reads it. Check with: node agent/redaction-audit.mjs --project <KEY>.
_nightShift: ROADMAP #3 / WF3: in the window (local time), once a night when idle: every known issue's regression test on main (KB1) and the knowledge lint; then the backlog (open tickets older than lookbackHours the agent never saw), at most maxTickets and maxCostUsd a night. The morning digest at digestAt on working days (weekends: true for every day). policy.json nightShift / morningDigest.
_presentation: The presentation (?present, ?deck; docs/PRESENTATION_PLAN.md). presenter, team, contact: on the first and the last slide (an empty value is left out). case: the one ticket shown whole, replayed from its recorded run (it must be in tourReplay too). live: the ticket asked live in Teams at the end. insights: the project shown on the Insights tab. ask: a recorded Ask answer of the case's project, replayed on the Ask tab (its question, as asked). system1: tickets where System 1 asked the reporter or took the light path. catches: what it caught that people missed (cross: a cause in another app; guard: a story whose commit the regression guard alerted on; review: a fix the AI review sent back; copies: a bug whose fix is missing in copies of its code).

presentation.ask: Why could http://localhost:4204/scadenze miss the doses due on Sunday?

_teams: Teams -> agent (ROADMAP #9, agent/README.md): approvers may approve or reject any fix by a reply under its 'fix ready' card, besides the person the card is for (a team lead; matched by the Teams display name, accents aside). project: the project of a question that names none (default: the pilot's). pollSeconds: how often the channel is read (15; 5 for a demo).
_baseline: Impact (WF5): the minutes each step takes the team WITHOUT the agent. Team estimates, not measurements, and the Impact tab says so. Hours saved = these minus the measured time, for a ticket's first analysis in a week, merged fixes and merged documentation.
_system1: System 1 (docs/SYSTEM1_PLAN.md): the local decision model. python and hfHome come from node demo/get-tools.mjs --only uv,laya; checkpoint is a fine-tuned model (agent/README.md, System 1). The server answers on 127.0.0.1:port only. Whether it is asked: policy.json system1.intake.

system1._startTimeoutSeconds: 125 s to load while a training ran on 2026-11-16 (10-40 s otherwise); a ticket that comes before the server is ready gets no System 1 answer
system1._gateWaitSeconds: the wait when an answer decides the path (askReporter, lightPath or privacy in auto, or a hold): BIL-26 got its answer 25 s after it was queued with another ticket, 2026-11-17

ask.question: Who knows the exemption code best?

insights._components: Hotspot map: a file belongs to the first component with a matching path prefix (tests count with their main code: src/test/java is read as src/main/java). Files outside every component are not counted.

_projects: One entry per Jira project and application repository; one watcher and one dashboard for all. A project entry overrides the settings above (insights, backendTestDir, …). stateDir: the project's agent state (default state/projects/<KEY>). app: ports of the running app (demo/run-mediagenda.mjs --project <KEY>). linked: the projects whose APIs the app calls; their code (read-only) and Jira tickets are part of every analysis. A project without a clone at repo is not watched.

projects._pilot: The pilot (demo/pilot.mjs tick, every 30 min): on working days, perDay changes with a hidden bug are pushed to main at the given hours, and the bug is reported in Jira reportAfterMinutes later. Scores against the answer key: node demo/pilot.mjs status.

pilot._reserve: cases kept for a live demo: the schedule never pushes or reports them; a person does (docs/PILOT.md, Live demo)
